# Open statements of the single proof

<!-- Generated by scripts/one_proof/render_open.py from open-statements.json (the Lean build), kinds.tsv and
claims.tsv. Do not edit by hand: edit kinds.tsv or claims.tsv, or regenerate the JSON after a fold. -->

`ZInQ.OneProof.frozenTarget` (`ZInQKernel/OneProof/Main.lean`) is a Lean theorem, checked by the kernel with no
`sorry` and only the standard axioms, that proves the frozen target `ZInQ.FrozenTarget` of Glazer's "Z is
Diophantine in Q" from the hypotheses below. Everything else is proved. Each hypothesis is a Lean `Prop`; proving
one in Lean, or reducing it to statements printed in the literature, removes it. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to contribute and check a proof.

**61 hypotheses of the H part** (in the bundles `OpenAddedLeaves11`, `OpenGlue7`, `OpenResearchLeaves12`, `OpenTextbookLeaves10`), plus 6 hypotheses of the Tian–Yuan–Zhang and Gross–Zagier parts listed at the end.

* **Strict count: 43 published / 18 glue** (the strictest flagged reading; 44/17 without the one strictest-reading flag).
* LEAF means a published, refereed theorem stated over genuine definitions in its printed form, or a consequence
  of it that is never stronger. GLUE is everything else: a consequence of one theorem, a composite of several,
  project glue, or a leaf whose published form is still pending a reading (`kinds.tsv`, column `flag`).
* By kind: composite 5, consequence 11, project glue 1, published 44.

### t09SymmIsogenyExists

* Bundle field `HDec.HSyn.OpenAddedLeaves11.t09SymmIsogenyExists`; kind **consequence**, strict **GLUE**.
* Source: Mumford 6, 8, 20, 23 (not splittable, av-split 4.1)
* Status: t09-pic: in progress: Pic0, phi_L, ample bundles, e_n (since 2026-11-14).

```lean
HDec.WeilPairing.T09_SymmIsogenyExists
```

> **T9 (restated over the definitions of §3).** Every abelian variety over a field carries a
> symmetric isogeny `λ : A → Â` to its dual, with Galois-equivariant perfect compatible Weil
> pairings. Published: Mumford §6 (Application 1: `A` is projective, so an ample `L` exists over
> `K`), §8 (`Â`), §13, §20 (the pairing `e_n`: bilinear, perfect, Galois-equivariant,
> `e_{mn}(x, y) = e_n(m x, y)`), §23 (`e^L_n(x, x) = 1`, so `λ = φ_L` is symmetric), and `φ_L` is an
> isogeny for ample `L` (§6, Application 1); Milne, *Abelian varieties* (Cornell–Silverman 1986)
> §§8-13, 16 (UNVERIFIED numbering). Take `D = (Pic⁰, e_n)`, `λ = φ_L`. Existential in `D`, hence a
> consequence, never stronger.

### thetaRatiosAlgebraic

* Bundle field `HDec.HSyn.OpenAddedLeaves11.thetaRatiosAlgebraic`; kind **composite**, strict **GLUE**.
* Source: Shimura 1976; Mumford Tata II IIIa 8; Igusa (qm-split: ThetaNullNonvanishing + glue, not folded)
* Status: igusa-alg: in progress: theta-glue reduced it to one leaf and five polynomial identities (since 2026-11-14).

```lean
HDec.HSyn.G0Split.ThetaPt.ThetaRatiosAlgebraic
```

> **LEAF candidate (theta-constant ratios are algebraic numbers).** For an abelian variety `A`
> over a number field `K`, a uniformization `Φ : ℂ² → A(ℂ)_σ` with kernel `Λ` and any period matrix
> `Ω ∈ 𝔥₂` of `Λ`: some theta constant `θ_{m₀}(0, Ω)` is nonzero and every ratio
> `θ_m(0, Ω)/θ_{m₀}(0, Ω)` is an algebraic number. This is the form in which the literature states
> it (values of Siegel modular functions with algebraic Fourier coefficients at a point whose
> principally polarized abelian variety is defined over `ℚ̄` are algebraic: Shimura, Duke 43 (1976);
> for genus 2 also Thomae's formula, Mumford, *Tata Lectures on Theta II*, IIIa §8; with
> `NS(A_ℚ̄) = NS(A_ℂ)` for the polarization defined by `Ω`; all locators UNVERIFIED). Nonvanishing:
> at most one of the ten even `θ_m(0, Ω)` vanishes in genus 2 (it vanishes exactly on products of
> elliptic curves; UNVERIFIED locator: Igusa 1962/1967). `ThetaNullAlgebraic` follows
> (`thetaNullAlgebraic_of_ratios`, proved).

### x6ConicModel

* Bundle field `HDec.HSyn.OpenAddedLeaves11.x6ConicModel`; kind **consequence**, strict **GLUE**.
* Source: Kurihara 1979; Elkies 1998 3
* Status: x6-fold: fold in progress (x6-glue) (since 2026-11-14).

```lean
HDec.X6Kummer.X6ConicModel
```

> **N2-L′ (leaf, new; the global form of `X6KummerModel`): `X₆ = X₀(6,1)` is the conic
> `Y² + 3X² + 3Z² = 0` with `π₆ = −16(X² + Z²)/(27 Z²)`, on `ℚ̄`-points of one witness.**
> 
> *Published statement* (Kurihara, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 25 (1979): `X₀(6,1) : x² + y² + 3 = 0`;
> Elkies, ANTS-III, LNCS 1423 (1998), §3: `X*(6) = X₆/W` with coordinate `t`, `t = 0, 1, ∞` at the
> CM points of discriminants `−24, −4, −3`, and `X₆ = X*(6)(√−t, √(3(t − 1)))`; locators
> UNVERIFIED, no network). Put `X = √−t`, `Y = √(3(t−1))`, `Z = 1`: then `Y² + 3X² + 3 = 0`,
> `t = −X²/Z²`, `W` acts by the sign changes, and `j = 16(t − 1)/27 = −16(X² + Z²)/(27 Z²)` is the
> coordinate of R2fp (`j = 0, ∞, −16/27` at `−4, −3, −24`; a Möbius map is fixed by three values).
> An isomorphism of `ℚ`-schemes `X₆ ≅ C` gives a bijection on `ℚ̄`-points commuting with
> `Aut(ℚ̄/ℚ)`, compatible with the maps to `P¹`. Consistency checks (VERIFIED by computation in
> `scratch/x6-kummer/conic_check.py`): the involutions `X ↦ −X`, `Y ↦ −Y`, `(X,Y) ↦ (−X,−Y)` fix
> exactly the two points over `j = −16/27`, `0`, `∞` respectively (Riemann–Hurwitz for a
> `(ℤ/2)²`-cover of `P¹` by a genus-0 curve); the residue fields there are `ℚ(√−3)`, `ℚ(i)`,
> `ℚ(√−3)`, as González–Rotger Thm 5.12 (the bundle's `R5ptProps`) requires for `ℤ[√−6]` (`b = 0`,
> `h = 2`), `ℤ[i]` (`b = 1`, `h = 1`, contains `ℚ(i)`), `ℤ[ζ₃]` (`b = 1`, `h = 1`, contains
> `ℚ(√−3)`); `C` and Kurihara's conic both correspond to `(−1, −3)_ℚ`, ramified at `{3, ∞}`. The
> fibre fields `ℚ(√−t, √(3(t−1)))` were checked against González–Rotger Thm 5.12 on all 24 rational
> CM points of Elkies' table by rv-nocm §1.3 Part B.

> **The newform case of R13 (GLUE: Kato's theorem for newforms, transported and dualized).**
> `EigenformHT` restricted to newforms. Needs, beyond Kato's printed statement (de Rham at `ℓ` with
> Hodge–Tate weights `0, k − 1` for `V_{F_λ}(f)`, cohomological normalization): the identification of
> any semisimple `ρ` attached to `f` (arithmetic Frobenius, trace `a_p`) with `V_{F_λ}(f)^∨`
> (Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt), and the negation of Hodge–Tate weights under duals. Not a leaf:
> `V_{F_λ}(f)` is not definable in Mathlib today.

### r16

* Bundle field `HDec.HSyn.OpenResearchLeaves12.r16`; kind **composite**, strict **GLUE**.
* Source: Shimura 1973 Thm 1; Shimura 1971 Thm 7.9; Diamond-Shurman
* Status: open: no one is on it.

```lean
LeafModCurves.R16_EichlerShimuraJ1'
```

> **R16. Eichler–Shimura in `J₁(N)`, existential form** (replaces the placeholder
> `R16_EichlerShimuraJ1`). Let `N ≥ 1`, `f ∈ S₂(Γ₁(N))` a newform with nebentypus `χ`, and `J` a
> Jacobian of `X₁(N)` over `ℚ` (`IsJ1`). Then `K_f` is a number field, and there are an abelian
> variety `A` over `ℚ`, a surjective homomorphism `π : J → A` over `ℚ`, and a ring homomorphism
> `θ : K_f → End⁰_ℚ(A)`, with `dim A = [K_f : ℚ]`, such that for every prime `ℓ` and every
> embedding `ι : K_f → ℚ̄_ℓ`: the `ι`-component of `V_ℓ(A)` has dimension 2, and for every prime
> `p ∤ Nℓ` and every arithmetic Frobenius `σ` at a place above `p`, `σ` acts on it with
> trace `ι(a_p(f))` and determinant `ι(χ(p))·p`.
> 
> Sources (a consequence of three published statements, none of them the zeta clause):
> (i) Shimura, J. Math. Soc. Japan 25 (1973), Thm 1, pp. 526-527, **unconditional clauses only**
> (quotient `A_f` of `J₁(N)` over `ℚ`, `K_f` acting, `dim A_f = [K_f:ℚ]`); its final Euler-factor
> clause carries an extra `Γ₀`/Fricke-stability condition and is **not** used here
> (`docs/research/locators.md`, row R16); (ii) `V_ℓ(A_f)` free of rank 2 over `K_f ⊗ ℚ_ℓ`
> (Shimura 1971 §7.4; Ribet 1977; UNVERIFIED locators); (iii) the Eichler–Shimura congruence
> relation `T_p = Frob_p + p⟨p⟩Frob_p⁻¹` on `J₁(N)` mod `p ∤ N` (Shimura 1971 Thm 7.9;
> Diamond–Shurman Thm 8.7.2; UNVERIFIED). The relation alone only gives an annihilating polynomial
> of Frobenius on each `ι`-component; the characteristic polynomial `X² − ι(a_p)X + ι(χ(p))p` of
> arithmetic Frobenius on the covariant `V_ℓ(A_f)`, `p ∤ Nℓ`, is printed as such in Diamond–Shurman
> Thm 9.5.4 and Shimura 1971 Thm 7.11 / Ribet 1977 (UNVERIFIED numbers; review finding 2026-11-12),
> which is the supplier to cite for the trace and determinant clauses.
> Shimura's theorems are for his canonical model of `X₁(N)`; they transfer to every model of §D
> because any two are `ℚ`-isomorphic (leaf MC9 of bp-modcurves: Shimura's canonical model for
> `Γ₁(N)` has function field `ℚ(j, f_{(0,1/N)})`, `ℚ`-isomorphic to `K_N`; Shimura 1971 §6.7,
> UNVERIFIED). If a convention gives `ā_p`, `χ̄(p)`, replace `θ` by `θ ∘ c` (`K_f` is totally real
> or CM, so complex conjugation `c` preserves it): the statement is unaffected.

### milneIsogenyQuasiInverse

* Bundle field `HDec.HSyn.OpenAddedLeaves11.milneIsogenyQuasiInverse`; kind **published**, strict **LEAF**.
* Source: fg = [d], gf = [d] as morphisms: Milne 1986 Rem. 8.4; Milne's notes Prop. 7.1; Mumford 7
* Status: cloud W17: briefed (CharZero form), after the two above (since 2026-11-14) [issue #81](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/issues/81).

```lean
AvSplit.MilneIsogenyQuasiInverse
```

> **LEAF (H-54; published form).** Milne, *Abelian varieties*, in Cornell–Silverman (eds.),
> *Arithmetic Geometry* (1986), §8, Remark 8.4 (UNVERIFIED number; also Milne's online notes
> *Abelian Varieties* (2008), Prop. 7.1 / Rem. 7.3, UNVERIFIED): "for an isogeny `f : A → B` of
> degree `n` there is an isogeny `g : B → A` with `g ∘ f = n_A` and `f ∘ g = n_B`", over any field.
> Specialization read off the same display: the degree `n` is weakened to "some `d ≥ 1`", the
> conclusion "`g` is an isogeny" is dropped, and the hypothesis "isogeny" is given as "finite and
> surjective" (`IsIsogenyMor`), which implies Milne's "surjective with finite kernel" (the kernel is
> the base change of the finite `f` along the zero section). `[d]_A` is `((d : ℤ) : End A)`, the
> `d`-fold sum of the identity in `Hom(A, A)`. Over an algebraically closed field this is also
> Mumford, *Abelian varieties* (1970), §7, Remark after Thm 4 (UNVERIFIED).

### shimuraTaniyamaQbar

* Bundle field `HDec.HSyn.OpenAddedLeaves11.shimuraTaniyamaQbar`; kind **published**, strict **LEAF**.
* Source: Shimura-Taniyama 1961 12.4 Prop. 26; Milne, CM notes 7 (model over Qbar)
* Status: open: no one is on it.

```lean
HDec.HSyn.G0Split.FibreQM.PeriodMapH.QMSplitSTQM.ShimuraTaniyamaQbar
```

> **LEAF (Shimura–Taniyama: abelian varieties with complex multiplication are defined over `ℚ̄`).**
> Let `A` be an abelian variety over `ℂ` (here of dimension 2) such that `End⁰(A) = ℚ ⊗ End(A)` contains a
> field `E` with `[E : ℚ] = 2 dim A` (an injective `ℚ`-algebra map `E → End⁰(A)`). Then `A` is isomorphic to
> `A₀ ×_{ℚ̄, ιe} ℂ` for an abelian variety `A₀` over `ℚ̄` and an embedding `ιe : ℚ̄ → ℂ`.
> 
> Sources: G. Shimura and Y. Taniyama, *Complex multiplication of abelian varieties and its applications to
> number theory*, Publ. Math. Soc. Japan 6 (1961), §12.4, Prop. 26; G. Shimura, *Abelian varieties with
> complex multiplication and modular functions*, Princeton 1998, §12.4, Prop. 26; J. S. Milne, *Complex
> multiplication* (notes), §7 ("abelian varieties with CM over `ℂ` are defined over `ℚ^al`"); all numbers
> UNVERIFIED (no network). Form: the printed statement with "CM" specialized to "a field of degree `2g` in
> `End⁰`" and `g = 2`; the printed conclusion is a model over a number field `L ⊂ ℂ`, and the `ℚ̄`-form is
> that model base-changed to the algebraic closure of `L` in `ℂ` (Milne prints the `ℚ^al` form).

### dsThm965

* Status: open: no one is on it.

```lean
ZInQ.Contrib.HodgeSplit.DSThm965
```

> **LEAF (Deligne's theorem, in Diamond–Shurman's form).** Diamond–Shurman, *A First Course in
> Modular Forms*, GTM 228 (2005), Thm 9.6.5 (for `k ≥ 2`; from Deligne, Sém. Bourbaki 355 (1969)
> [the Bourbaki talk, publ. 1971], and Shimura 1971 Thm 7.14 for `k = 2`; numbering UNVERIFIED): for a
> normalized eigenform `f ∈ S_k(N, χ)`, `k ≥ 2`, and `λ ∣ ℓ` in `K_f`, there is a continuous
> `ρ_{f,λ} : G_ℚ → GL₂(K_{f,λ})`, unramified at every `p ∤ ℓN`, such that for every maximal ideal `𝔭`
> of `ℤ̄` over `p` the arithmetic Frobenius `Frob_𝔭` has characteristic polynomial
> `x² − a_p(f) x + χ(p) p^{k−1}`. Lean form: coefficients extended along `K_{f,λ} → ℚ̄_ℓ` given by
> `ιL ∘ ιC⁻¹` (the place `λ` is the one `ιL ∘ ιC⁻¹` induces), places of `ℚ̄` as valuation subrings,
> arithmetic Frobenius as pkg-I4's `IsArithFrob`. The semisimplicity of the row is not part of this
> form (Ribet 1977 gives irreducibility; here it is the glue `Semisimplification2`).

> `K` a field with a discrete valuation ring `O`, `w` a valuation ring of `K̄` over `O`, `A/K` an
> abelian variety. Then (a) ⟺ (b) ⟺ (c), where (a) good reduction at `O`, (b) for every `m ≥ 1`
> invertible in `O`, inertia at `w` fixes `A(K̄)[m]`, (c) the same for infinitely many such `m`.

### igusaGL2

* Bundle field `HDec.HSyn.OpenTextbookLeaves10.igusaGL2`; kind **published**, strict **LEAF**.
* Source: Igusa's theorem: the Galois image on E_j[N] over Q(j) is GL_2(Z/N) (Igusa, Amer. J. Math. 81 (1959); Lang, Elliptic functions Ch. 6 3)
* Status: cloud W14: briefed (via X0Transitive), not yet claimed on the issue (since 2026-11-14) [issue #83](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/issues/83).

```lean
ZInQ.RLeaf.IgusaGL2
```

> **Igusa's theorem** (published), as usually stated: the Galois representation of
> `Gal(\overline{ℚ(j)}/ℚ(j))` on `E_j[N]` is surjective onto `GL₂(ℤ/N)`, in every basis.
> 
> Source: Igusa, Amer. J. Math. 81 (1959); Lang, *Elliptic functions*, Ch. 6, §3; for any model of
> the generic curve over `ℚ(j)` (numbers UNVERIFIED). The geometric image is `SL₂(ℤ/N)` for every
> model, because the monodromy of a family over the `j`-line maps onto `PSL₂(ℤ)` and `PSL₂(ℤ)` does
> not lift to `SL₂(ℤ)`; the determinant is the cyclotomic character, onto `(ℤ/N)^×` over `ℚ(j)`.

* Bundle field `HDec.HSyn.OpenTextbookLeaves10.mumfordTorsionAlgClosed`; kind **published**, strict **LEAF**.
* Source: A(k)[n] = (Z/n)^{2g} over k algebraically closed, char k not dividing n: Mumford, Abelian varieties 4, Application 2 (iv)
* Status: cloud W16: briefed, not yet claimed on the issue (since 2026-11-14) [issue #81](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/issues/81).

```lean
AvSplit.MumfordTorsionAlgClosed
```

> **LEAF (H-25; published form).** Mumford, *Abelian varieties* (1970; 2nd ed. 1974), §4,
> Application 2, (iv) (UNVERIFIED locator): for an abelian variety `X` of dimension `g` over an
> algebraically closed field `k` and an integer `n` with `char k ∤ n`, the group
> `X_n = {x ∈ X : nx = 0}` of `n`-torsion points is isomorphic to `(ℤ/nℤ)^{2g}`. Mumford's points
> are the closed points, i.e. the `k`-points (`Pts A k`); `dim` is the topological Krull dimension
> of the underlying space; "`char k ∤ n`" with `n ≥ 1` is `(n : k) ≠ 0`; the group isomorphism is a
> bijection `e` with `e(x + y) = e x + e y` (written multiplicatively on points).

> Mathlib's (equivalent to Stacks' smoothness, Stacks 00T7 / 00TA).

> **LEAF (Chia-Fu Yu, *Endomorphism algebras of QM abelian surfaces*, J. Pure Appl. Algebra 217 (2013),
> Thm 1.1, journal p. 907; arXiv:1210.1125 Thm 1.1; the journal first page was read by the locator audit,
> `docs/research/locators.md` row T27; volume number UNVERIFIED).** Let `A` be an abelian surface over an

> conclusion). `End⁰(A) = ℚ ⊗_ℤ End(A)` (`PkgI3.AbVar.End0`) over the kernel's abelian varieties
> `PkgI3.AbVar`; the division hypothesis is "every nonzero element is a unit"; indefinite is
> `QuatIndefinite a b` (`0 < a ∨ 0 < b`), the same hypotheses as the row.
